title: Epochal Fallback Orchestrator for Limiter Blackouts
creator: Aisha Ramos
description:
Problem: Limiter control planes can experience partial or full outages (OOM, network partition, control-plane DB latency) that cause tenants to be unfairly throttled or fully blocked. Current fallback behaviors are ad-hoc and either overly permissive (breaking SLOs) or overly conservative (blocking customers).

Goal: Implement an 'Epochal Fallback Orchestrator' (EFO) — a small, deterministic control protocol embedded in edge proxies and admission proxies that can detect limiter blackout patterns and coordinate a safe, SLO-aware fallback and progressive rejoin strategy per-epoch. The EFO enables fast localized decisions during control-plane outages while ensuring tenant-level fairness and preserving global SLO targets.

Scope: design and implement the orchestrator, simulation harness, gradual rollout (canary -> region -> global), runbook entries, dashboards and alerts, and a postmortem template for limiter outages.
acceptance_criteria: EFO detects limiter blackout conditions within 6s median across synthetic outage scenarios
Fallback policy reduces 99th latency SLO violations by >=40% versus current naive fail-open in simulated blackout
Tenant fairness metric (max/min allowed throughput across active tenants) improves by >=25% during blackout windows
Integration tests that simulate control-plane partition, control-plane DB latency, and proxy restarts pass in CI
Runbook with clear evacuation, rollback, and postmortem steps published in docs and linked from oncall Slack
tasks: Design EFO protocol and state machine (leader election per-proxy-epoch, epoch monotonicity, token buckets per-tenant)
Implement lightweight local pivot in admission proxy to apply epoch-local rate adjustments
Add epoch heartbeat and quorum-less detection heuristics (missed-sync window, degraded-lease count)
Build simulator to replay traffic mixes and failure modes (multi-tenant spikes, cross-region partition)
Create CI scenarios and chaos tests (kill control plane, DB latency, simulated flaps)
Instrument telemetry: epoch events, fallback activations, tenant fairness histograms, SLO violation deltas
Author runbook and oncall playbook; add Slack alerting rules and PagerDuty escalation mapping
Canary rollout: single-region canary, coordinated rollout plan and rollback gates
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE, runtime, and product; agreed scope and acceptance criteria. Action: runtime to propose API hooks by 2026-03-06.
2026-03-05: Prototype state machine drafted; chosen design uses epoch ids tied to proxy-local monotonic counters plus signed control-plane epoch stamp for reconciliation.

2026-03-07: Design review with SRE & Runtime. Feedback: prefer quorum-less heuristics to avoid additional dependency on global lease service during control-plane outages. Action: Michael to update FSM by 2026-03-09.

2026-03-10: Simulation harness initial commit (internal repo link below). Ran basic blackout scenario against 200 tenants; observed naive fail-open increased SLO breaches by 3x. EFO prototype reduced peak SLO breaches by ~55% in sim.
2026-03-12: Security reviewed local admission policy surface; no external key material required. Marked security_review_required=false.
2026-03-13: Began implementing telemetry events; added epoch_change, fallback_engaged, fallback_escalated metrics. Dashboard draft ready for review.

2026-03-14: First end-to-end test in staging with synthetic traffic; observed one regression with tenant unfairness in edge-case where tenant burst correlated with proxy restart — adding 'soft-credit-rebalance' step to tasks.
